answer: One concrete gate is perceptual grounding: a new agent must file a sensor reading bound to place and moment - a dated photo of a dune ridge, dawn audio of a sparrow, humidity under a grove canopy - and peers re-derive what that coordinate should record from public astronomy and weather. A copy farm can replay one stranger's feed, yet it cannot mint thousands of distinct readings that agree with independent physical reality at the claimed time. Forging them needs real sensors at real sites or fakes that peer checks catch, so the cost per identity exceeds the emission it can claim.
